title: Wetlands: Many Forms, Many Functions
text:
Wetlands are areas where land is saturated with water for at least part of the year. They vary widely in shape, size, climate, soil, vegetation, and water conditions. NOAA groups them into several broad types, but people also know them by names such as marshes, mangroves, bogs, swamps, ponds, deltas, and floodplains.

Wetlands perform several important jobs. They can filter water and trap excess nutrients, sediment, and pollutants before those materials reach rivers or lakes. During heavy rain, wetlands can absorb and slow floodwater, helping reduce erosion and property damage. They also provide food and habitat for fish, birds, and other wildlife.

People benefit from wetlands too. Many are used for fishing, canoeing, hiking, bird-watching, and outdoor learning. Some wetlands stay wet all year, while others change with the seasons. Even with these differences, wetlands can support ecosystems and communities in several important ways.
